sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown (📊) cache: invalidate it for columns whose cells are populated asynchronously, after the initial render. The WIP.1 cache keys off which rows are currently visible, which cannot see a column that fills previously-empty cells in place with no row show/hide — so a dropdown opened while such a column was still loading would cache a near-empty bundle that nothing ever refreshed (until an unrelated filter or sort happened to change the visible-row signature). New table-wide `_invalidateUniqDropDataCacheForTable(table)` is now called from `initReleaseEventsColumn()` (both post-population re-scan sites), `initRelationshipsColumn()`'s completion handler, and `initPicardTaggerColumn()`; `_artSetInlineSortKey()` additionally invalidates just its own column, since it stamps the `.mb-inline-art-sort-key` sentinel that the dropdown's inline-artwork scan reads, from ~8 CAA/EAA fetch-completion callbacks. Affects the Release events / Release country / Release date, Relationships, Picard tagger and inline CAA/EAA columns.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 4 (`openUniqDrop()` per-open caching): the unique-values dropdown's 5 full `tbody.rows` scan passes (whole-cell value counts, flag-icon segment map, relationship-cell detection, relationship icon counts, inline CAA/EAA-thumbnail counts) are now cached per (table, column) in a `WeakMap`, keyed by a cheap O(rows) signature of the currently visible rows' `data-mb-row-idx` values. Reopening the same column's dropdown with no filter/sort change in between skips straight past all 5 passes. Measured on `artist-events` (4174 rows, 21 columns, median of 5, script 9.99.970 both sides, captured back-to-back on one machine): warm dropdown open 31 347 ms → 581 ms (**54x faster**), with global filter (1242→1292 ms), column filter (1201→1239 ms) and sort (2995→2906 ms) all unchanged within noise. Cold (first) open is unchanged within noise too — 30 649 → 32 985 ms, against an observed ~20% run-to-run spread for that same 30-second 5-pass scan; a cache miss adds only one O(rows) signature build plus one `Map.set`. Each Map/counter declaration became a `_uniqCacheHit ? … : <original>` ternary in place and each scan loop got a `!_uniqCacheHit` guard, so none of the hundreds of `.set()`/`.get()`/`++` call sites inside the loop bodies changed. Keying by the live `<table>` element means a brand-new table (new fetch, disk-load, multi-table sub-table) is always a cache miss, with no manual reset needed.

Landed WITHOUT PERFORMANCE.org Step 3, which it was originally written alongside: `_updateAllColHeaderCounts()` — the function Step 3 caches — is never reached from `openUniqDrop()`, so it contributes nothing to the win above. The one thing Step 4 genuinely needed from Step 3, the shared `_visibleRowSetSignature(table)` helper, is carried here standalone; a later Step 3 can key off the same primitive unchanged.

Found and fixed one correctness gap while implementing: the "Cell structure" section's collapsed/expanded split is read from `expandedCells` (individually-toggled cells), not derivable from the visible-row signature, so a lone cell expand/collapse click would otherwise leave a reopened dropdown showing a stale split. Added `_invalidateUniqDropDataCache(table, colIndex)` and wired it into all 5 places `expandedCells` is mutated by user interaction (`_applyCollapseState()`'s two branches, `ensureCollapseDelegate()`'s three inline toggle branches).

Found and fixed a second gap that the earlier `perf-steps-1-4` / `perf-steps-3-4` versions of this change still carry: 10 further symbols populated inside the (now skipped) first scan pass were neither defaulted from the cache nor stored into it — `editorDeletedValueCounts`, `editorAnyDeletedCount`, `editorRecordedNameValueCounts`, `editorMembershipValueCounts`, `editorCommentValueCounts`, `changelogHasMessageCount`, `changelogNoMessageCount`, `releaseQualityHighCount`, `releaseQualityLowCount`, `releaseQualityNormalCount`. Left as-is they read 0/empty on every warm reopen, silently dropping the "🗑️ any deleted editor", "📜 has changelog message", "🚫 no changelog specified" and "🟢/🟠/⚪ data quality" entries plus every Editor-info value entry — and, since those same counters gate their sections' visibility conditions, potentially collapsing a whole section to empty. Affects the `annotations` pageType (Editor / Version history columns) and every page carrying a "Release" column. Same failure mode as the previously-recorded `roleTokenValueCounts` miss.
